## Purpose
The rules tables: configured rules, user-defined rule categories, per-agent rule assignments, and the rule event log.

## Responsibilities
- **`Rule` (`rules`):**
  - `id`: a slug, e.g. "agent.read_only_database";
  - `scope` (agent or workflow, indexed), `type` (a `RULE_TYPES` key), name and description;
  - `params` (JSON) and `enforcement` (block, warn or fix; default block);
  - `always_on`, `enabled` and `source` (recommended or user);
  - `category`, and `targets` (a JSON list of agent ids or workflow names);
  - the timestamps.
- **`RuleCategory` (`rule_categories`):** id, name, description, color (default slate), icon (default Tag), scope, `rule_types` (JSON), default_enforcement, default_applies (always or ai) and created_at.
- **`RuleAssignment` (`rule_assignments`):** agent_id, rule_id, source (ai or user) and reason. It is unique on `(agent_id, rule_id)`.
- **`RuleEvent` (`rule_events`):**
  - rule_id, rule_name (a snapshot), scope and subject_id;
  - `checkpoint`: creation, message, tool_call, answer, run, validate or step;
  - `outcome`: passed, blocked, warned, fixed or applied;
  - message, detail (JSON), conversation_id, execution_id, step_id and created_at (indexed);
  - the index `ix_rule_event_subject` covers `(scope, subject_id, created_at)`.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **A workflow's rule selection lives on its definition** (`WorkflowDefinition.rules`), not here. Agents live on Mistral, so their selection needs a table.
